meta.title_plain: How a croquet club built the world's oldest tennis tournament
meta.teaser: Wimbledon began in 1877 with 22 players. Here's how its traditions stuck.

page.title: How a croquet club built the world's oldest tennis tournament
page.bigIdea: Wimbledon started in 1877 with just 22 players. It still plays on grass and wears white, because some traditions are worth keeping.

cards.title: It started with croquet
cards.back: The club began in 1868 as the All England Croquet Club. In 1876 it added a brand-new game called lawn tennis. A year later, it held a championship.
cards.tryit: Invent a mini game with a ball and two cups. Play it for 10 minutes and write down its rules.

cards.title: 22 players, lots of rain
cards.front: The very first Wimbledon was tiny.
cards.back: In 1877, only 22 men entered. Rain delayed the final by four days. Spencer Gore won it in 48 minutes, with about 200 people watching.
cards.tryit: Count how many players are in your tennis club or group. Is it more or less than 22?

cards.title: Grass cut to 8mm
cards.front: Why does the grass matter so much?
cards.back: Wimbledon is the only Grand Slam still played on grass. The grass is grown fresh from seed every year and cut to just 8mm tall.
cards.tryit: Find a ruler and look at 8mm. Then bounce a ball on grass and on a hard floor. Which bounces lower?

cards.title: Why everyone wears white
cards.back: In Victorian times, sweat stains were seen as rude, and white hid them. Since 1963 players must wear mostly white. Since 1995, almost entirely white.
cards.tryit: Look at photos of other big tournaments. Count how many colours you see compared with Wimbledon.

cards.title: Strawberries and cream
cards.front: The most famous snack in tennis.
cards.back: Strawberries are in season right when Wimbledon happens. Fans eat about 28,000 kg of them. They're picked the day before and arrive around 5:30am.
cards.tryit: Ask your family about one food tradition you always have at a special event. Where did it start?

words.d: One of tennis's four biggest tournaments each year.

quiz.q: What game was the Wimbledon club first set up for?
quiz.hint: Look at the club's very first name.
quiz.why: It began in 1868 as the All England Croquet Club, and added tennis in 1876.

quiz.q: In 1877, 22 men played. Today the men's singles has 128 players. About how many times bigger is that?
quiz.hint: Round 22 to 20, then ask how many 20s fit into about 120.
quiz.why: 128 ÷ 22 is about 5.8, so it's roughly 6 times bigger.

quiz.q: Why did players start wearing white?
quiz.hint: Think about what shows up on a shirt after a long, hot match.
quiz.why: In Victorian times sweat stains were seen as improper, and white clothes hid them best.

quiz.q: Spencer Gore won the 1877 final in 3 sets and 48 minutes. On average, how long was each set?
quiz.hint: Share the 48 minutes equally between the sets.
quiz.why: 48 ÷ 3 = 16, so each set took about 16 minutes on average.

page.think: Wimbledon keeps its old traditions but added a roof and electronic line calls. If you ran a tournament, what would you keep and what would you change?
